I checked out privacytools.io - found some good info and system tests there - thanks for the link!

Depends a bit on what you're doing and what you're priorities are. For myself, the following are "must haves":
- AdBlock: for obvious reasons
- Flashblock: less necessary these days, IMO, but still a nice-to-have.
- Ghostery: One of the great privacy tools. Identifies and provides blocking-services for a variety of webtrackers.
- HTTPS Everywhere: Automatically forces an encrypted connection for most sites.
- Privacy Badger: A bit redundant with Ghostery and AdBlock, but is another tool for blocking trackers and ads.
- Reddit Enhancement Suite: Hmm...guess I don't really need this anymore. ;)

I'd replace AdBlock by Ublock. Ublock is more memory efficient and they don't have companies paying them to whitelist their adds. I started using it a few weeks ago and I'm noticing a lot less adds than with Adblock.
MyWot - this thing has saved me from very malicious sites

There have already been named very good ones, i'll try to add the one's I additionally use.

  • Discovered µBlock a few days ago, trying it out for a few days now, seems to hold up pretty good
  • I use Disconnect instead of Ghostery, since I've read about some controversies about it, so I went with Dc.
  • If you're active on twitch.tv, I recommend BetterTTV. It's a must have in my opinion.
  • I occasionally watch YouTube videos, and Subscriptions Grid For Youtube helps me sort my videos better. (If you like grid views that is)
  • Stylish, pretty neat if you find some cool userstyles. I use one to color the progressbar of my YouTube videos differently

• uBlock origin - the best adblocker out there
  • WoT - for knowing if a site is ok
  • Disconnect - no more 3rd party trackers
  • Tweetdeck Enhancer/Moderndeck - if you use tweetdeck
  • HTTPS everywhere
  • Block Misspelled Websites
  • BugMeNot
LastPass Great password storage system because it never actually stores your password anywhere.

If you use Reddit or Voat, use Hoverzoom, it displays all those imgur pictures linked from Reddit/Voat as a pop-up when you hover over the link. I've used the whitelist mode though as it can sometimes be annoying on other websites.

I have just two primary add-ons that I can't live without:

  • Tabs Outliner which helps me deal with my 30 tabs+ at times by showing them in a nice tree style, and allowing me to save them for later almost like a temporary bookmark.

  • µBlock is a much better alternative to AdBlock/ABP - faster, no weird deals with ad companies, and the developer is very fast to respond (I've reported a few bugs)

I'm extremely careful about choosing Chrome Extensions due to the amount I deal with Bitcoin sites; (a little bit of a PSA here for anyone that cares) there have been plenty of extensions which the owners sold, and then the new owners silently updated the extension with bitcoin-stealing malware (i.e. it would attempt to withdraw your coins from sites like Blockchain and Coinbase when you visited them)
Lights out for YouTube is useful, it dimms out everything when you go in theater mode.
